title: Shortest way through mazes
prompt:
Read from standard input one or more mazes, separated by one or more empty lines. A maze is a block of lines of equal length made of `.` (free), `#` (wall), `S` (start) and `E` (exit), with exactly one `S` and one `E`. Moving one cell up, down, left or right through free cells (the cells `S` and `E` are free too) takes one step; you cannot leave the maze or cross walls.

For the k-th maze (counted from 1) print `Maze k: N`, where N is the smallest number of steps from `S` to `E`, or `Maze k: no path`.
